definition: Entrepreneurial means having the drive and imagination to start and run new businesses.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word entrepreneurial. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know entrepreneurial should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Even as a hospital custodian, Vanna had an entrepreneurial eye: she noticed the night-shift vending machines always sat empty and won the contract to restock them herself.
A self-starting employee begins work without being told; entrepreneurial reaches further - starting not just tasks but whole ventures.
An enterprising scout finds clever ways to sell the most cookies; entrepreneurial goes a step beyond, naming the drive to build and run new businesses outright.

Venturesome stresses the appetite for risk - willingness to try undertakings that might fail. Entrepreneurial needs that appetite but adds the builder's eye: noticing the unmet need and organizing a business around it. A venturesome investor backs someone else's idea; an entrepreneurial founder builds her own.

Ambitious people want to rise - a bigger title, a harder goal, a larger stage - whatever the field. Entrepreneurial points that hunger at one target: spotting a gap and building a new venture to fill it. An ambitious lawyer chases partnership; an entrepreneurial one opens her own firm.

Entrepreneurial means having the drive and imagination to start and run new businesses.
When streaming emptied her video store, the owner refused to wait for the customers to come back.
She opened a phone-repair counter, then a board-game cafe in the freed-up aisles, then a rental service for party equipment.
Each venture was small; together they showed an entrepreneurial instinct for spotting the next gap before the last business closed.
Entrepreneurial is more specific than 'driven' or 'hardworking': it names the particular drive to spot an opportunity and build a new venture around it, risks and all.
Entrepreneurial praises initiative pointed at building something new, usually a business.
Enterprising is the broader compliment for resourcefulness anywhere; proactive, its unit-mate, is initiative aimed at preventing problems rather than launching ventures.
Reach for entrepreneurial when the story involves spotting a market gap and taking the risk to fill it.

Nobody in Prem's village asked for a refrigerated warehouse, which is precisely why he noticed there wasn't one.
Every June, tomato prices collapsed for two frantic weeks and farmers dumped what they could not sell; every August, the same tomatoes tripled in price.
Prem was twenty-three, employed, and by his own account comfortable.
He leased a diesel cold room, bought June tomatoes at a fair price, and sold them in August.
Economists would call it arbitrage; his mother called it entrepreneurial to the bone: he had seen a gap nobody else treated as a business and organized one around it.
Six villages now sell to his warehouses, and the June dumping has quietly stopped.
